info.desc: Hunky Dory is the fourth studio album by English musician David Bowie, released on December 17, 1971, through RCA Records. Compared to the guitar-driven hard rock sound of his 1970 album, The Man Who Sold the World, Bowie opted for a warmer, more melodic piano-based pop rock and art pop style on Hunky Dory. His lyrical concerns on the record range from the compulsive nature of artistic reinvention on "Changes", to occultism and Nietzschean philosophy on "Oh! You Pretty Things" and "Quicksand"; several songs make cultural and literary references. He was also inspired by his stateside tour to write songs .

podcast.body: Released 13 months after "The Man Who Sold the World," this album marked a significant step forward for Bowie, giving him another hit with the song "Changes." The album was a clear sign that "something was happening" with Bowie's career after years of searching for his niche. "When the Hunky Dory album came out, Bowie had become friends with Mark Bowen, a former folkie who had taken up electric guitars and formed a psych band called T-Rex."

podcast.body: This album, released in late 1971, marked Bowie's debut on the RCA label and showcased the first real evidence of his commercial potential. It won favor on US rock stations and cracked the Billboard album chart in early 1972, peaking at number 176. The album also featured tracks like "Oh! You Pretty Things" and "Queen Bitch" which played with queer iconography, complementing Bowie's emerging androgynous identity. "These songs, including Life on Mars and Changes, would appear on his late 1971 album, Hunky Dory. Bowie's debut on the RCA label and the first real evidence of his commercial potential."
